title: The Yorker Premium: Does Royal Challengers Bengaluru Gain More from Execution or Variation?
dek: At the death, is Royal Challengers Bengaluru's best weapon the perfectly executed yorker or the well-disguised slower ball? Commentary labels let CricField price both.
excerpt: Across the IPL since 2022, the yorker has cost less per ball in the death overs than slower balls and cutters. Here is how Royal Challengers Bengaluru's delivery mix compares.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Execution or Deception
body: Death bowling has two philosophies. One says nail the yorker and the batter cannot score; the other says change pace and the batter cannot time it. Both are skills, and both carry a cost when they go wrong.

Using commentary-derived labels for deliveries in overs sixteen to twenty since 2022, the league's yorkers cost {{ev:yk-rest-yorker}} runs per ball, slower balls and cutters {{ev:yk-rest-slower}}, and all other labelled deliveries {{ev:yk-rest-other}}.

sections.heading: Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Mix
body: Yorkers make up {{ev:yk-share}} of Royal Challengers Bengaluru's labelled death deliveries, against {{ev:yk-lshare}} for the rest of the IPL.
When they land it, RCB concede {{ev:yk-team-yorker}} per yorker; slower balls and cutters cost them {{ev:yk-team-slower}}.

sections.heading: Building the Death Plan
body: The data favours execution over variation at league level. The practical answer is a mix: a bowler whose yorker is reliable should lead with it, and a bowler whose yorker misses should lean on pace-off deliveries.
That makes yorker accuracy in practice a measurable selection input, not just a coaching talking point.

sections.heading: What Labels Cannot Capture
body: Commentary labels describe the result as much as the intention: a slower ball that is smashed may be recorded as a full toss. That bias could make either option look better than it is.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Execution First, Variation as Cover
body: For Royal Challengers Bengaluru, the league evidence says the yorker is the cheaper death ball when bowled. The bowling plan should be built around whichever each bowler executes more reliably.
Tracking each bowler's delivery mix and cost by type each season would turn this from instinct into measurement.

methodology: Regulation innings only (super overs excluded). Economy uses runs charged to the bowler (byes and leg-byes excluded) per legal ball times six. Bowler wickets exclude run outs. Slower balls include off- and leg-cutters.
